subject: Renewal & consolidation: perimeter tooling (WAF/CDN) recommendation
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: API perimeter consolidation - initial ask

Team,

I'm starting a consolidated renewal review for our perimeter stack (WAF, CDN, gateway). Current contracts with Cloudflare and Fastly roll in Q1; Akamai is an occasional fallback for specific customers. We're exploring a consolidation that reduces overlap, improves observability, and gives us clearer unit economics.

Attached is a workbook with current usage and cost breakdowns (gateway_cost_model_v3.xlsx) — please review the assumptions tab. High-level asks:
- Can each of you validate the traffic/feature assumptions by Tuesday (23 Nov)?
- Marissa: can you draft a vendor scorecard template I can use to grade proposals?
- Vivek: any operational constraints we should flag (SLA, log retention, edge compute differences)?

Goal: pick a pragmatic two-vendor posture (primary + hot-standby) with clear migration checkpoints so engineering and security have time to test.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Head of Platform Procurement (acting)
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: gateway_cost_model_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 420KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: API perimeter consolidation - initial ask

Diego — thanks for kicking this off. I cleaned up the scoring template and attached a draft vendor_scorecard_Q4.pdf. I scored each vendor by category (cost, WAF efficacy, latency impact, SSO/SCIM, procurement friction, roadmap). Quick notes:

- Cloudflare: strongest feature set for WAF and bot management; good CDN footprint in EU/US; licensing model is a bit opinionated for our gateway/worker usage.
- Fastly: great for edge compute and real-time VCL customizations; CDN pricing can be favorable at high commit; historically higher engineering integration effort.
- Akamai: very robust enterprise controls and peering; commercial terms are typically less flexible and longer lead times.

Two questions for the team:
1) Are we comfortable moving WAF + CDN primary to one vendor if we keep Fastly for edge compute (for product features)?
2) I recommend we ask each vendor for: one-year committed pricing, a signed SOC2/ISO pack, and a sample SLA amendment for token redaction/log retention.

I'm available to run vendor calls Wed/Thu afternoon next week.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Procurement
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: vendor_scorecard_Q4.pdf (PDF, 85KB)

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@cloudflare.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cloudflare Sales <sarah.nguyen@cloudflare.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Cloudflare proposal for Redwood (RF-2026-07)

Hi Diego / Marissa —

Thanks for the heads-up and the scorecard. We've reviewed your workbook and attached a short proposal (cloudflare_proposal_RF-2026-07.pdf). Highlights:
- Discounted committed tier for CDN + WAF when combined under one contract; proposed 12-month term with an option to toggle worker capacity.
- Offer: 18% off list for a 12m commit with $250k minimum spend, plus 30-day pilot pricing for a month.
- We can provide SOC2 Type II report and custom SLA terms (redaction & log access) — link to Docusign and evidence in the proposal.

We can set up a technical call with our edge product engineer to discuss log formats and KV cache semantics on Thurs (26 Nov) at 10am PT.

Best,
Sarah Nguyen
Account Executive, Cloudflare
sarah.nguyen@cloudflare.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@cloudflare.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cloudflare proposal for Redwood (RF-2026-07)

Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround and the pilot offer. A few items we need to validate before moving to commercial terms:
1) Evidence: SOC2 Type II, penetration test summary, and an archive of audit logs for a 30-day window (we have customers that require 12-month retention but we'll scope that separately).
2) Tech: We need clarity on log ingestion formats (JSON vs NDJSON), log latency, and any required change to our KV cache usage if we migrate gateway sessions.
3) Contract: we've had to limit vendor data retention in prior contracts; can you share a standard SLA amendment that includes a clause for token redaction and a 72-hour incident response for P1s?

Marissa/Vivek — once we have vendor artifacts I'll schedule a legal + security review block for the week of Dec 6. Laura, please confirm procurement timing; we'd like to align exec approval with the Dedicated renewal cycle.

Thanks,
Diego

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Recommendation: perimeter tooling posture and next steps

Team,

Summary of recommendation after reviewing proposals and the pilot telemetry:
- Primary for WAF+CDN: Cloudflare (best fit for WAF capability, global coverage, and consolidated observability).
- Keep Fastly for edge compute features where VCL/custom compute provides product differentiation.
- Akamai: maintain as a contractual fallback for specific enterprise customers but do not consolidate primary traffic there.

Commercial ask: accept Cloudflare's 12-month commit with the proposed discount, but add two contract conditions before signature:
1) SOC2 Type II and a penetration test summary delivered to Redwood legal/security within 7 business days of intent to sign.
2) Add SLA amendment for log retention & token redaction and a 72-hour P1 response paragraph.

Operational next steps:
- Marissa: secure updated proposal with DocuSign link for legal review (target 03 Dec).
- Diego: schedule tech sign-off and migration playbook (engineering + security dry run) for week of Dec 13.
- Laura: confirm spend authorization process and whether this needs exec-level approval.

I'll open a procurement ticket in HubSpot (deal RF-2026-07) and link the Drive folder. If there are no objections, I'll instruct procurement to move forward with Cloudflare as primary and set Fastly as a retained supplier for edge-only features.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference
